properties.name: spatial
properties.appliesTo: all elements except internal table elements, internal ruby elements, and inline boxes

values.name: none
values.prose: No effect.

values.name: page
values.prose: Establishes a limited front spatial context, which allows spatial positioning in front of the element’s plane. (However, see front-limit for limits on this area.)

values.name: portal
values.prose: Establishes two spatial contexts connected by a portal coinciding with the border box of the spatial container: a back spatial context behind the element consisting of a 3-dimensional “world” with its own independent coordinate system, which can be viewed through the spatial container’s portal (which acts as a window into this “world”). a front spatial context, which allows relative spatial positioning in front of the element’s plane just like page does, as well as behind it by extending through the portal into the the “world” of the back spatial context.

properties.name: portal-stage
properties.appliesTo: spatial containers establishing a back spatial context
properties.computedValue: as specified, but with lengths made absolute

values.name: <length>
values.prose: The stage expands from the world origin by the specified length towards the indicated side. Values can be negative.

values.name: auto
values.prose: The stage expands from the world origin to contain the contents of the back spatial context on the indicated side.

properties.name: portal-transform
properties.appliesTo: spatial containers establishing a back spatial context
properties.computedValue: as specified, but with lengths made absolute
properties.animationType: Discrete if the presence of the none or auto keyword differs; otherwise interpolate each <transform-list> independently, see CSS Transforms 1 § 9 Interpolation of Transforms.

values.name: none
values.prose: The world origin of the back spatial context is the center of its border box on the portal plane, and the portal transform ensures that <length> values correspond between the page and the back spatial context (i.e. 1cm in the back spatial context is 1cm on the page.)

values.name: auto
values.prose: The matrix required to fit the containing volume (or bounding sphere of the containing volume, in the case of portal-action: orbit) of the back spatial context into an axis-aligned rectangle whose sides align with content edges of the spatial container, and front aligns with the portal plane. If a <transform-list> is specified before auto, then it is applied to the containing volume prior to this calculation.

values.name: <transform-list>
values.prose: The back spatial context is transformed as specified.

properties.name: portal-action
properties.value: none | orbit || resize || [ pan | pan-inline || pan-block || pan-x || pan-y || pan-z ]
properties.appliesTo: spatial containers establishing a back spatial context

values.name: none
values.prose: The contents of the back spatial context cannot be repositioned or rotated by the user.

values.name: orbit
values.prose: The contents of the back spatial context can be rotated around the center of the containing volume by the user.

values.name: resize
values.prose: The contents of the back spatial context can be resized (scaled) by the user.

values.name: pan
values.prose: The contents of the back spatial context can be translated (in any direction) by the user.

values.name: pan-inline
values.prose: The contents of the back spatial context can be translated (in the specified page-aligned axis) by the user.

values.name: pan-block
values.prose: The contents of the back spatial context can be translated (in the specified page-aligned axis) by the user.

values.name: pan-x
values.prose: The contents of the back spatial context can be translated (in the specified page-aligned axis) by the user.

values.name: pan-y
values.prose: The contents of the back spatial context can be translated (in the specified page-aligned axis) by the user.

values.name: pan-z
values.prose: The contents of the back spatial context can be translated (in the specified page-aligned axis) by the user.

values.name: spatial-absolute
values.prose: This module introduces the spatial-absolute keyword to the position property. When contained by a spatial container, this value takes the now spatially positioned box out of flow and positions it into the containing volume of the back spatial context (in the case of spatial: portal), or the front spatial context (in the case of spatial: page) of its spatial container.

properties.name: inset-back
properties.appliesTo: positioned boxes contained by a spatial container
properties.percentages: for relative spatial positioning, relative to the distance from the containing block to the front limit plane; for absolute spatial positioning, relative to the z-axis size of the containing volume.

values.name: auto
values.prose: If both insets in this axis are auto, then the box is positioned at its default z-axis position. Otherwise, this value defers positioning to the opposite inset, see below.

values.name: <length-percentage>
values.prose: The box’s position is inset by the specified amount from the front (for inset-front) or back (for inset-back).

properties.name: inset-front
properties.appliesTo: positioned boxes contained by a spatial container
properties.percentages: for relative spatial positioning, relative to the distance from the containing block to the front limit plane; for absolute spatial positioning, relative to the z-axis size of the containing volume.

values.name: auto
values.prose: If both insets in this axis are auto, then the box is positioned at its default z-axis position. Otherwise, this value defers positioning to the opposite inset, see below.

values.name: <length-percentage>
values.prose: The box’s position is inset by the specified amount from the front (for inset-front) or back (for inset-back).

properties.name: position-area
properties.newValues: [ front | center | back | span-front | span-back | span-all ]? | origin

values.name: origin
values.prose: This module also extends the <position-area> syntax to allow the origin keyword everywhere that center is currently allowed. This value represents a (zero-sized) track that coincides with the anchor’s origin, and its area-specific default alignment is anchor-origin.

properties.name: z-align-self
properties.value: auto | <overflow-position>? [ normal | front | center | back ] | anchor-origin

values.name: container
values.prose: The used anchor box of the default anchor box is its axis-aligned bounding box in the coordinate system of the positioned box’s containing block/containing volume, and the position-area grid is likewise oriented in the coordinate system of its containing block/containing volume.

values.name: anchor
values.prose: The positioned box is transformed together with its default anchor box. The anchor box is used directly in the default anchor box’s own coordinate system, however that has been transformed, and the position-area grid is likewise re-oriented. The positioned box moves, rotates, and scales together with the default anchor box. What should be the effective containing block used to calculate the position-area grid? Is it just transformed along with the anchor box (simple but maybe not very useful), or is it independently intersected somehow?

properties.name: environment-map
properties.appliesTo: elements participating in a back spatial context

values.name: none
values.prose: The environment map is opaque black in all directions.

values.name: auto
values.prose: The environment map used is the user agent’s default environment map.

values.name: <dashed-ident>
values.prose: The environment map is defined by the @environment-map rule matching the specified name (if any; otherwise it is opaque black).

properties.name: environment-intensity
properties.appliesTo: elements participating in a back spatial context

properties.name: environment-rotate
properties.appliesTo: elements participating in a back spatial context

atrules.name: @environment-map
atrules.prose: Environment maps are named and defined using the @environment-map at-rule, which contains a list of environment map descriptor declarations. Its syntax is as follows:

values.name: equirectangular
values.prose: The rectangular image is mapped onto the interior of a sphere (similar to a Mercator projection), with the top of the image coinciding with the y-most point on the sphere, the bottom of the image coinciding with the y-least point on the sphere, and the center of the image at the z-least point on the sphere (directly in front of the user). If more than one source image is provided, the first one is used and all others are ignored.

values.name: cube
values.prose: The six images provided in the src descriptor are mapped onto the interior of an axis-aligned cube, see § 6.1.1.1 Mapping Images Onto a Cube.

warnings.name: auto
warnings.prose: The existing offset-anchor and transform-origin properties can change the object origin. Specifically, the effective object origin for CSS positioning and alignment (see below) is the origin defined by offset-anchor, which defaults to the origin defined by transform-origin—​which itself gains a new initial value of auto (matching the syntax of offset-anchor) to represent the default behavior specified above.

warnings.name: front
warnings.prose: This module extends the <anchor()> syntax to add front and back to <anchor-side>. Together with the existing start/end keywords, this allows the inset-front and inset-back inset properties to resolve against the corresponding sides of the anchor box.

warnings.name: back
warnings.prose: This module extends the <anchor()> syntax to add front and back to <anchor-side>. Together with the existing start/end keywords, this allows the inset-front and inset-back inset properties to resolve against the corresponding sides of the anchor box.

warnings.name: depth
warnings.prose: Similarly, for sizing purposes, the <anchor-size()> syntax gains a depth keyword to represent the z-axis size of the anchor box. (Note the thickness of a CSS box, unless otherwise defined, is zero.)

warnings.name: origin
warnings.prose: It also adds an origin keyword to <anchor-side>, which resolves against the object origin of the anchor box.

warnings.name: anchor-origin
warnings.prose: This module also introduces the new anchor-origin value, which centers the origin of the alignment subject against the origin of its default anchor box. When anchor-origin is specified, the inset properties behave differently in the affected axis: instead of adjusting the inset-modified containing block, they shift the origin of the alignment subject—​exactly as if it were a zero-sized containing block and the effective origin were the resulting inset-modified containing block.
